nodes.title: 🏷️ NOVA TAG WRITER - HOW ROWS FIND FILES
widgets_values:
🔗 MATCHING
-----------

Rows match files by the filename_column value (FileName here), treating
case, spaces and underscores as equal:
No Cage But Mine.flac = No_Cage_But_Mine.flac = NO CAGE BUT MINE.FLAC
Files with no matching row are listed at the end of the log and left
completely untouched. A partial database cannot damage the rest of the
folder.


🔤 COLUMNS BECOME TAGS AUTOMATICALLY
------------------------------------

Lowercased, separators removed: Track Number -> tracknumber,
EncodedBy -> encodedby. Four exceptions:
* Length            (skipped by default - duration is read from the audio stream, it is not a settable text field)
* the filename col  (it is the match key, not a tag)
* skip_columns      (anything you list here)
* column_map        (anything you remap; Column = skip drops it)

*** THE GREY TEXT IN column_map IS ALSO A PLACEHOLDER ***
EncodedBy = encoded-by / Comment = description / Copyright = skip
is an example. While it looks filled in the field is EMPTY and the
automatic mapping is used. Click in and type to make it real. The proof
is in the results log: its Tags line reads
Comment -> comment, not Comment -> description.


🧪 RUN WITH dry_run ON FIRST
----------------------------

dry_run produces the identical log - every file, every tag, every value
- and opens nothing for writing. Read it, then turn it off.

nodes.title: 📊 READING THE RESULTS
widgets_values:
The log opens with what it is about to do. Read that part first:
* Database / Table  (where the rows came from, and how many)
* Batch             (the folder, and the file count)
* Matching          (which column is being used as the match key)
* Tags              (THE MAPPING IT ACTUALLY USED. A column_map entry missing from this line did not take effect)

Then one line per file with the tag count written, and finally
* Processing complete!  (tagged=13  skipped=0)

tagged + skipped should equal your file count. When skipped is not zero
the names are listed - nearly always a filename_column value that does
not match the file on disk.


📤 OUTPUTS
----------

* written_count / skipped_count  (numbers, wire them onward)
* files                          (the batch passed straight through)


✅ VERIFY IN THE SAME RUN
-------------------------

Nova Tag Writer > files > Nova Tag Reader > console > Nova Console reads
back from disk what was just written.


⚠️ IT WRITES, IT NEVER REMOVES
------------------------------

Setting a tag replaces that tag and leaves every other tag alone.
So renaming one through column_map (EncodedBy = encoded-by) on a file
that already carries ENCODEDBY ADDS the new key beside the old one. You
end up with both. Clearing the leftover needs a separate step - this
node has no way to express a deletion today.

Requires mutagen.

nodes.title: 🏷️ NOVA AUDIO TAG WRITER
widgets_values:
Writes metadata from a database table onto the matching audio files. One row per file. 
The files are edited IN PLACE.


🧠 NO DATABASE YET? START HERE
------------------------------

* Copy examples/nova_album_example.db -out of the pack to somewhere of your own, point database_path at the copy, table_name albums, column_set tags.
* Three example rows come back and nothing touches your audio - this node only reads. 
* Then edit the rows in DB Browser for SQLite (free, sqlitebrowser.org) like a spreadsheet. 
* FileName must match the file on disk; that is how a row finds its file. 
* The node's own help page has the longer version.


🧩 TWO INPUTS, BOTH REQUIRED
----------------------------

Nova SQLite Reader    > table   the rows (what to write)
Nova Batch Load Audio > files   the batch (what to write it onto)


⚙️ SET THESE FOR YOUR OWN DATA
-------------------------------

* database_path  (Full path to an existing .db, note that a path that does not exist is an error, not a silent create)
* table_name     (The table holding one row per track)
* columns        (* for all, or a comma-separated list e.g. title, artist, album)
* folder_path    (Loads the folder of audio files)
* file_filter    (*.flac here, Comma-separated globs e.g. *.flac, *.wav, *.ogg)


🔥 THE GREY TEXT IN where field IS A PLACEHOLDER, NOT A FILTER 🔥
-----------------------------------------------------------------

Artist = 'crazy gecko' AND Genre LIKE '%Metal%'  ⚠️ is an example hint, while it looks filled in, the field is EMPTY and every row is returned. 

* Click in and type to make it real and check record_count against what you expected before you write anything.


📝 WHY decode_audio IS OFF
--------------------------

* Tagging works on file paths and never reads a waveform, decoding the folder would cost minutes of CPU and gigabytes of RAM for a result nothing reads.

✅ Leave decode_audio it off for tagging.

* The database is opened read-only. This side cannot alter your data.
